# 1. Select a specific patient's longitudinal records up to year 2
patient_data <- longitudinal_data[longitudinal_data$patient_id == "Patient_101" & 
                                  longitudinal_data$observation_time <= 2, ]

# 2. Compute dynamic predictions (conditional on surviving past year 2)
pred_joint <- predict(jm_renal, newdata = patient_data, process = "both",
                      times = seq(2, 10, by = 0.1))

# 3. Generate the unified Joint Plot
# This automatically displays the eGFR trajectory on top and the survival curve below

library(survival)
library(nlme)
library(JMbayes2)

# Transform standard data into competing risks multi-state format
# Assume 'status_factor' is a factor variable with levels: "censored", "ESKD", "death"
baseline_competing <- crData(baseline_data, statusVar = "status_factor")

# Inspecting this data reveals new columns: 'status' (0 or 1) and 'strata' (the event type)
head(baseline_competing)


# 1. Fit the longitudinal eGFR model (same as before)
lme_egfr <- lme(eGFR ~ observation_time * cohort + age,
                random = ~ observation_time | patient_id,
                data = longitudinal_data)

# 2. Fit the Cause-Specific Survival sub-model
# 'strata(strata)' creates distinct baseline hazards for ESKD vs. pre-ESKD Death
cox_competing <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ strata(strata) * (cohort + baseline_proteinuria),
                       data = baseline_competing, 
                       x = TRUE, model = TRUE)

# 3. Fit the Competing Risks Joint Model
# 'jm' automatically pairs the eGFR path to both event types
jm_competing <- jm(cox_competing, lme_egfr, time_var = "observation_time")

# View summaries including separate Association Parameters (alpha) for each risk
summary(jm_competing)



# 1. Isolate historical data for a specific patient up to year 3
patient_profile <- longitudinal_data[longitudinal_data$patient_id == "Patient_305" & 
                                     longitudinal_data$observation_time <= 3, ]

# 2. Predict future risk conditionally past year 3 for BOTH competing events
pred_cif <- predict(jm_competing, newdata = patient_profile, process = "event",
                    times = seq(3, 10, by = 0.1), return_CIF = TRUE)

# 3. Generate the plot
# This generates stacked cumulative incidence lines tracking ESKD risk vs. Death risk over time
plot(pred_cif)
